title: Performance, caching, limits, scale testing, and graceful degradation
objectives: Explain Salesforce performance as throughput under governor limits, not only CPU time.
Place Platform Cache (session versus org partitions) against transactional statics and against skipping SOQL.
Use Scale Center, ApexGuru, and Scale Test in Full sandbox as official observability and scale-testing tools.
Define graceful degradation: keep the critical path working when a cache miss, async queue delay, or non-critical dependency fails.
diagnostic_question: A LAB_ pricing LWC is slow at month-end close, hits CPU, and a non-critical recommendation callout times out. Before you add indexes or more Apex, which of performance, caching, limits, scale testing, or graceful degradation do you apply first—and in which environment?
definition: On Salesforce, performance is how many concurrent requests complete in time while staying inside platform governor limits. Caching (Platform Cache partitions, plus in-transaction statics) reduces repeat SOQL. Scale testing uses Scale Test in a Full sandbox to simulate production load before go-live. Graceful degradation keeps core work available when a non-critical dependency fails. ([Well-Architected Reliable](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/reliable); [Platform Cache Partitions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_cache_partition_setup.htm))
why_it_matters: Candidates who only recite CPU time miss throughput, selective SOQL, cache partitions, and Full-sandbox scale tests. Interviewers also want a degradation story: if recommendations time out, quote still saves. Limits exist because the platform is multitenant; they are a design input, not an insult.
sixty_second_explanation: Treat month-end like an ER surge. Governor limits are the number of beds: they protect every tenant, not just you. Platform Cache is the crash cart already counted so you do not run to the pharmacy (SOQL) for the same supply list. Scale Center is the occupancy board; Scale Test is a drill in a Full sandbox that looks like the real ward. Graceful degradation is diverting non-urgent consults so trauma still gets a bay.
deeper_explanation: Well-Architected Reliable defines throughput as concurrent requests completed in a time interval. Solutions designed for throughput stay inside governor limits. Focusing only on maximum CPU time misses bulkification, selective SOQL, async offload, and cache. ApexGuru (in Scale Center) flags SOQL/DML in loops and missed cache opportunities. ([Well-Architected Reliable](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/reliable))

The Lightning Platform Cache holds session and org data in partitions so one app does not steal another app's space. Create partitions in Setup; use Cache.Session / Cache.Org (and CacheBuilder) from Apex. Session cache is per user session; org cache is shared. Allocations are whole numbers, zero or five or greater per segment, summing to org capacity. Partitions are not auto-pulled into packages. ([Platform Cache Partitions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_cache_partition_setup.htm); [Well-Architected Reliable](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/reliable))

Scale Center shows long-running transactions, exception hotspots, and throughput bottlenecks. Scale Test simulates large UI/API workloads before production; Well-Architected Resilient maps performance and scale testing to Full sandbox (not Developer sandbox). Exact governor numbers live in the Execution Governors and Limits table—reverify for the API version; do not invent a private cheat sheet in the interview. ([Well-Architected Reliable](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/reliable); [Resilient environment strategy](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/resilient); [Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm))

Graceful degradation is failure mitigation in Reliable/availability language: classify what is critical, keep a basic path working, and do not let a non-critical callout or cache miss fail quote save. Async is favored to protect synchronous CPU, but Scale Test in Full sandbox is how you learn whether queue latency is acceptable. Cache is not a source of truth; on miss, query and refill.

mental_model.analogy: Hospital ER surge plan: beds are governor limits; crash-cart inventory is Platform Cache; occupancy board is Scale Center; Full-sandbox drill is Scale Test; diverting non-urgent consults is graceful degradation.
useful_mapping: governor limits → finite beds on a shared ward (multitenant)
throughput → patients completed per hour, not one CPU lab test
Platform Cache org partition → shared supply list
Platform Cache session partition → one patient's chart on the tray
ApexGuru → flags of SOQL-in-loop 'running to pharmacy each pill'
Scale Center → occupancy and hotspot board
Scale Test in Full sandbox → surge drill with production-like volume
graceful degradation → trauma bay stays open if the gift shop POS dies
where_it_breaks: Cache is not durable storage; a miss is expected.
Full sandbox data volume still may not match production skew—Needs verification per org.
Governor tables change by context (sync vs async); quote the live table.
The analogy does not encode LDV indexes or ownership skew (ARCH-003).

claims.claim: Well-Architected Reliable treats throughput (concurrent completed requests) as the performance lens. CPU time is only one governor. ApexGuru flags SOQL/DML in loops and missed cache opportunities.

Platform Cache uses partitions with session and org segments so apps do not steal each other's capacity. Allocations are whole numbers, zero or five-plus per segment. Partitions must be packaged explicitly.
claims.validation: Platform Cache Partitions plus Reliable cache guidance.

claims.claim: Governor limits protect multitenant shared resources. Quote numbers only from the current Execution Governors and Limits table for the execution context.
Performance and scale testing belongs in a Full sandbox. Scale Test simulates production-like UI/API load before production deploy. Scale Center surfaces long-running transactions and bottlenecks.
claims.validation: Resilient environment table plus Reliable Scale Test/Center.

claims.claim: Availability of solutions built on the platform is a shared responsibility. Architect for failure mitigation: keep critical paths working when non-critical dependencies fail (graceful degradation), and validate async latency tradeoffs with Scale Test.
claims.validation: Reliable availability and async tradeoff notes.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Performance is throughput inside governors, not only CPU. Cache partitions cut repeat SOQL. Prove load with Scale Test in a Full sandbox. If a non-critical callout dies, still save the quote.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from the critical user path. I bulkify and make SOQL selective, then cache stable reference data in a named partition. I read Scale Center/ApexGuru instead of guessing. I refuse Developer sandbox as a scale-test stand-in. I design a degraded mode: skip recommendations, queue the callout, do not fail LAB_Quote__c save. I open the governors table rather than reciting last year's numbers.

terminology.plain: How fast and how many requests finish without tripping limits.

terminology.example: Month-end LAB_Quote__c save stays under CPU and SOQL while 200 users work.
terminology.non_example: A single debug log that looks 'fast' with one row.
terminology.boundary: Query selectivity details overlap ARCH-003 LDV.

terminology.plain: Remembering data you already fetched so you do not query it again.
terminology.precise: Platform Cache session vs org partitions, plus in-transaction statics. CacheBuilder checks cache then SOQL. Not a system of record.
terminology.example: Org cache of LAB_Price_Book_Flags__mdt for the day.
terminology.non_example: Storing every Account in cache as the database.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Event bus: messages, not a cache.
terminology.boundary: Partition capacity and TTL are org-specific.

terminology.plain: Per-transaction caps so one tenant cannot exhaust the shared pod.
terminology.precise: Documented in Execution Governors and Limits. Sync versus async contexts differ. Multitenant architecture explains why they exist.
terminology.example: Too many SOQL in a loop throws a limit exception.
terminology.non_example: A contractual SLA with a customer.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Feature licenses: commercial, not transaction governors.
terminology.boundary: Always cite the live table in an interview if asked for a number.

terminology.plain: Proving the design with production-like volume before production.
terminology.precise: Scale Test in a Full sandbox simulates UI/API load. Well-Architected maps performance/scale testing to Full sandbox, not Developer sandbox.

terminology.non_example: Clicking Save twice in a Developer sandbox.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Unit tests: correctness, not pod-scale throughput.

terminology.plain: The important action still works when a side feature fails.

when_to_use: When a feature is slow or throws limits: start with performance as throughput, then caching and governors—not a bigger CPU myth.
When the same reference data is read across transactions: Platform Cache partitions, not Visualforce view state.
When you must prove a peak-season design: scale testing in a Full sandbox with Scale Test / Scale Center, not a Developer sandbox click-through.
When a non-critical dependency fails: graceful degradation so the core save still commits.
when_not_to_use: Do not use Platform Cache as the system of record or to hide non-selective SOQL on huge volatile data.
Do not treat governor limits as optional or as a request to Salesforce Support to 'raise CPU' as the architecture.
Do not run scale testing in a Developer sandbox and call it production-like.
Do not call a data-integrity failure graceful degradation; integrity errors must still fail the transaction.

options.B: Both are durable like custom objects
options.C: Org cache is only for files

mcqs.rationale: Cache Partitions: session for individual sessions, org for data any users can access.

distractor_explanations.B: Cache is in-memory, not a database.

interview_questions.question: How do you talk about Salesforce performance without only saying CPU?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Throughput: completed concurrent requests inside governors. Bulkify, selective SOQL, cache, async. CPU is one limit among many.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use Well-Architected Reliable language. I mention ApexGuru anti-patterns. I refuse 'raise the limit' as architecture. I point at Scale Center evidence. I keep LDV indexes in ARCH-003 unless asked.
interview_questions.example: LAB_QuoteService is the Scale Center hotspot at month-end close.
follow_ups: Where do you get limit numbers?
weak_answer_warnings: Reciting a blog's CPU number as eternal truth

interview_questions.question: Explain Platform Cache partitions.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Named slices of session and org cache so apps do not steal capacity. Allocate whole numbers, zero or five-plus. Package partitions explicitly. Miss means query.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I cache stable reference data, not every Account. I use CacheBuilder. I do not use view state as a cache. I check org capacity. I never cache secrets.
interview_questions.example: LABPricing org partition for flag metadata.
weak_answer_warnings: Cache as the system of record

interview_questions.question: Month-end quotes are slow and a recommendation callout flakes. Design it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Fix bulk/SOQL, cache flags, degrade recommendations, scale-test in Full sandbox.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Critical path is quote save. I bulkify, cache metadata, and isolate the callout so timeout does not addError the quote. I use Scale Center to confirm the hotspot moved. I schedule Scale Test in Full sandbox before peak. I will not call a Developer sandbox a load test.
follow_ups: How do users see pending recommendations?
weak_answer_warnings: Fail the save when the banner 500s

interview_questions.question: A teammate wants to scale-test in a Developer sandbox this afternoon. Your answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: No. Well-Architected maps performance and scale testing to Full sandbox. Developer sandbox lacks production-like volume.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I explain scratch/dev for build, partial for UAT, Full for scale. Refresh cadence on Full is slow, so we plan it. If we lack a Full sandbox, I say that gap is an environment-strategy risk (ARCH-011), not a reason to fake a load test.
interview_questions.example: Peak-season Scale Test rehearsal runs only on a Full sandbox.
tradeoffs: Full sandbox cost versus production incident cost

interview_questions.question: CPU limit on a trigger. Walk the diagnosis.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Scale Center/ApexGuru for loops and extra SOQL. Bulkify. Consider async after commit. Do not start by asking Support to raise CPU.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I reproduce with bulk rows, not one record. I check recursion and extra Flow. I look at cache misses that turned into SOQL storms. I open the governors table for trigger context. I only then consider splitting work. Lock issues belong to ARCH-008 if the error is row lock, not CPU.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Quote__c after-save plus helper in a loop.
weak_answer_warnings: The limit is a Salesforce bug

interview_questions.question: Production cache seems empty after a package install. Cause?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Partitions are not auto-included in packages. Runtime validation means compile succeeded and cache misses.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I check Setup partitions in the subscriber org and the package contents. I add partitions to the package and a post-install check. I confirm keys include namespace. I do not blame CacheBuilder first.
interview_questions.example: LABPricing partition missing after unlocked package upgrade.
weak_answer_warnings: Apex cannot see cache so the feature is impossible

interview_questions.question: When is caching the wrong performance move?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When data is highly volatile, user-specific and sensitive, or the real issue is non-selective SOQL on huge tables. Cache will not fix a table scan.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I cache reference data. I do not cache other people's Opportunities in org cache. I fix indexes and filters (ARCH-003) for LDV. I do not use cache to store secrets. If every transaction must see the latest Qty, that is locking (ARCH-008), not cache.
interview_questions.example: Inventory Qty is a lock problem; price-book flags are a cache candidate.

interview_questions.question: Teach performance, cache, limits, scale testing, and graceful degradation with one picture.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: ER surge: beds are limits, crash cart is cache, occupancy board is Scale Center, Full-sandbox drill is Scale Test, diverting gift-shop POS failure is degradation.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I then break it: cache is not the pharmacy warehouse, Full sandbox may still lack production skew, and governors must be read from the table. Interviewers want the Full-sandbox choice and a quote that still saves.
